research.abstract: Abstract Sex-determining systems in flatfishes are highly diverse, and even closely related species can differ in both sex-determining loci and heterogametic systems. In common dab ( Limanda limanda ), the genetic basis of sex determination has not yet been established. Here, we investigated sex determination using pooled whole-genome sequencing combined with long-read genome sequencing of females and males from Iceland and Norway. Genome-wide allele-frequency analyses identified sex-associated regions consistent with male heterogamety (XX/XY), with the strongest signal on chromosome 16. Comparison of the existing reference assembly, which represents an X haplotype at this locus, with a haplotype-resolved male PacBio HiFi assembly revealed a ∼21.5 kb Y-specific insertion on chromosome 16. The insertion showed complete coverage in male pools but little or no coverage in female pools from either population. It contained a translocated genomic segment including a copy of gonadal soma-derived factor ( gsdf ) and a predicted gene of unknown function. Comparative genomic analyses were consistent with this segment originating from an autosomal gsdf -containing region on chromosome 1. Given the recurrent recruitment of gsdf as a sex-determining factor in teleosts, we designate the Y-linked copy gsdfY and identify it as the strongest candidate for the master sex-determining gene in common dab. Additional broad sex-associated differentiation on chromosome 19 was restricted to the Icelandic samples and may reflect population-specific expansion of the sex-linked region, although its structural basis remains unresolved. Together, these findings provide the first genomic characterization of sex determination in common dab and demonstrate how gene duplication and translocation can contribute to the evolution of novel sex-determining systems in flatfishes.

The minimum inhibitory concentrations of five NRDs - bedaquiline (BDQ), clofazimine (CFZ), delamanid (DLM), pretomanid (PMD) and linezolid (LZD) - were determined using the broth microdilution method. Risk factors for NRD resistance were identified using Firth's penalized logistic regression. Whole-genome sequencing (WGS) was performed on 99 isolates, including all NRD-resistant strains and randomly selected susceptible strains, to analyze resistance-conferring mutations, phylogeny, and clustering. RESULTS: Among 561 people with MDR/RR-TB, resistance proportions were BDQ 4.3%, CFZ 3.6%, DLM 1.1%, PMD 1.1% and LZD 1.4%. BDQ exposure posed a higher risk of both BDQ- and CFZ-resistance than CFZ exposure. Based on the WHO mutation catalogue, WGS predicted NRD resistance with 100% specificity, sensitivity ranged from 16.7% to 75.0%. Notably, 37.5%-66.7% of resistant cases had no prior NRD exposure, and clustered isolates indicated transmitted resistance. CONCLUSION: NRD resistance among MDR/RR-TB patients in Shenzhen remains low. Although prior drug exposure is the primary risk factor, there is also evidence of transmitted resistance. NRD surveillance is essential to guide treatment and control transmission.

research.abstract: Introduction Abutilon fruticosum Guill. & Perr. is a drought-tolerant Malvaceae subshrub native to Saudi Arabia. However, no mitochondrial genome has previously been reported for the genus Abutilon . This study reports the first complete mitochondrial genome of A. fruticosum and evaluates its comparative and phylogenetic relationships within Malvaceae. Methods The mitochondrial genome was assembled, annotated, and analyzed for genome composition, repetitive sequences, codon usage, predicted RNA-editing sites, nucleotide diversity, synonymous and nonsynonymous substitution rates, collinearity, and phylogenetic relationships inferred from 32 shared mitochondrial protein-coding genes across ten taxa. Results The mitogenome was assembled as a circular molecule of 826,313 bp, with a GC content of 44.94%, and contained 37 protein-coding genes, 3 rRNA genes, and 21 tRNA genes. Comparative analyses of five Malvaceae mitogenomes revealed conserved codon-usage patterns, with weak-to-moderate bias influenced by nucleotide composition and functional constraints, but substantial variation in repeat abundance and distribution. DeepredMT predicted 397 RNA-editing sites in A. fruticosum , fewer than in Tilia amurensis , Gossypium trilobum , and Hibiscus cannabinus , but slightly more than in Adansonia perrieri . Simple sequence repeats and short dispersed repeats predominated, whereas G. trilobum had the greatest proportion of long repeats and H. cannabinus the highest repeat density. Nucleotide-diversity hotspots were detected in rpl16 , rps3 , cox2 , and rpl2 , while most protein-coding genes had dN/dS values below 1. The elevated dN/dS signal in rps4 suggested accelerated evolution or relaxed functional constraint, warranting further investigation. Maximum-likelihood analysis recovered A. fruticosum (tribe Malveae) as sister to the sampled Hibiscus – Gossypium clade with strong support. Discussion This study presents the first mitochondrial genome of Abutilon , expanding mitogenomic resources for Malvaceae. The A. fruticosum mitogenome shows conserved gene content and codon usage, alongside lineage-specific variation in repeat organization, predicted RNA-editing sites, nucleotide diversity, and localized sequence divergence. The phylogenetic placement is consistent with the accepted classification of A. fruticosum in Malvoideae and illustrates the potential of mitogenomic data for systematic studies within Malvaceae, although broader taxon sampling is needed to test this placement. This mitogenome provides a resource for marker development, population-genetic studies, comparative mitogenomics, and phylogenetic research on Abutilon and related Malvaceae lineages.

research.abstract: BACKGROUND: Tuberculosis caused by members of the Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex (MTBC) poses significant threats to animal health, public health, and wildlife conservation. Mycobacterium orygis, an emerging MTBC member, remains poorly characterized with respect to its epidemiology and transmission dynamics among Indian wildlife and livestock. METHODS: Fifty-five necropsy tissue samples from 21 captive wild animals were subjected to mycobacterial culture and a panel of molecular diagnostic assays, including multiplex PCR, Xpert-Ultra, and Truenat MTB/Rif. Confirmed MTBC isolates were characterized by drug susceptibility testing (GenoType MTBDRplus) and spoligotyping. Six isolates were selected for whole-genome sequencing (WGS), and phylogenetic analyses were performed against publicly available reference genomes. RESULTS: Of 55 samples, 38 were MTBC-positive and 6 yielded nontuberculous mycobacteria. Drug susceptibility profiling revealed 28 pan-susceptible isolates, nine with isoniazid monoresistance, and one with rifampicin monoresistance. Spoligotyping classified 10 isolates as CAS1-Delhi, 27 as orphan lineages, and one remained unassigned. WGS of six isolates, representing diverse host species and tissue types, identified four as M. tuberculosis (CAS1-Delhi lineage). Notably, one orphan isolate from a blackbuck was reclassified as M. orygis. Phylogenetic analysis revealed that this M. orygis strain was genetically distinct from other Indian wildlife strains and most closely related to a human-derived isolate from Karnataka, suggesting cross-host genomic relatedness. The remaining isolates clustered with Indian and global reference genomes; one was closely related to cattle-derived strains, whereas four were more closely related to human-derived strains. Low pairwise SNP distances (0-78 SNPs) with strong bootstrap support indicated close genomic relatedness across host species and geographic regions. CONCLUSION: This study shows the MTBC genomic diversity among various hosts. The phylogenetic relationships suggest that there is genetic relatedness among host populations such as M. orygis in a captive Indian blackbuck, which was in human contact for a long time. The study demonstrates the importance of integrated One Health genomic surveillance of mycobacterial infections at the human-animal interface and calls for more extensive, epidemiologically linked studies to look for cross-host transmission pathways.

research.abstract: Abstract Understanding how species diversity originates, accumulates and is sustained across heterogeneous regions is a core goal of macroevolutionary and conservation biology. The genus Huperzia is an ancient and cosmopolitan lineage of lycophytes, with species widely distributed in both temperate alpine and subtropical low‐ to mid‐elevation areas, offering ideal material for investigating the diversification history of early vascular plant lineages. Here, we utilized 87 plastid genomes from 23 species to reconstruct a robust phylogenetic framework within Huperzia and found that the development of the petiole and midrib should be considered supplementary diagnostic characters in future taxonomic revisions. Our spatiotemporal and spatial phylogenetic analyses indicated that temperate and montane regions, especially northeastern China and parts of the Qinghai–Tibet Plateau, preserve phylogenetically distinctive paleo‐lineages, whereas subtropical evergreen broad‐leaved forests contain younger lineages associated with ecological expansion and trait differentiation. This niche transition was accompanied by repeated leaf‐trait differentiation and shifts in plastid‐gene selection in subtropical lineages, with three positively selected genes ( rps19 , chlB and atpH ) identified by branch‐site analyses. This evolutionary strategy provides a new perspective for understanding how early vascular plants maintained a dynamic equilibrium between refugial conservatism and adaptive innovation.

research.abstract: Abstract Introduction Spondylodiscitis is an infectious condition involving the intervertebral disc and adjacent vertebral bodies. Although Staphylococcus aureus and Mycobacterium tuberculosis are the most common pathogens, cases caused by Gram-negative bacilli are relatively rare. Enterobacter hormaechei is an exceptionally uncommon etiologic agent in this context. Case presentation A 69-year-old Turkish male with type 2 diabetes mellitus and a history of prostate adenocarcinoma in remission, with no active immunosuppression, presented with lower back pain and elevated inflammatory markers. Initially suspected to have metastatic spinal involvement, spinal MRI revealed spondylodiscitis at the T12–L1 level. Microbiological evaluation of the needle biopsy specimen yielded Enterobacter hormaechei . Species-level identification was established by culture and MALDI-TOF MS, with off-label syndromic PCR testing (BIOFIRE ® Joint Infection Panel) providing supportive concordant results. The patient was successfully managed with surgical intervention and appropriate antimicrobial therapy. Discussion Spondylodiscitis due to Enterobacter hormaechei remains exceedingly rare. This case highlights the importance of considering atypical Gram-negative organisms in spinal infections and underscores the value of advanced microbiological methods for accurate species-level identification.

research.abstract: Purpose: To evaluate whether fluorescence lifetime imaging ophthalmoscopy (FLIO) combined with deep learning can detect metabolic signatures for classification of type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). Design: Cross-sectional analysis of participants included in the AI-READI dataset (version 3) with FLIO imaging. Subjects: 1,783 participants from the AI-READI dataset (version 3) with HbA1c measurements and FLIO imaging scans: 425 normoglycemic, 569 prediabetic, and 789 diabetic. Methods: Glycemic groups were defined from self-reported diagnosis, glucose-lowering medication, and HbA1c. Center-of-mass mean lifetime ({tau}CMM) maps, corrected for background and system timing offset, were generated from the raw time-resolved FLIO scans. Group differences in central-window {tau}CMM were tested by one-way ANOVA and by age-adjusted analysis of covariance. Convolutional neural networks (CNNs), ResNet-18, and XGBoost were trained on {tau}CMM maps for three-class (normal, prediabetic, diabetic) and two binary (normal vs. impaired; normal vs. diabetic) classification of T2DM and compared them with an age-only classifier and with models combining FLIO and age. Main Outcome Measures: Macro-averaged area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC), sensitivity, specificity, accuracy, F1 score, and positive predictive value (PPV). Results: Group-averaged {tau}CMM was longer in prediabetic and diabetic than in normoglycemic participants in both the SSC (p < 0.001) and the LSC (p < 0.001), but only the SSC difference remained significant after age adjustment (p = 0.017). For 3-class classification, the CNN using FLIO achieved the highest AUROC (0.60 +/- 0.04), compared with 0.51 +/- 0.03 for an age-only classifier. ResNet-18 and XGBoost showed similar performance. Binary classification of normal vs. diabetic participants yielded AUROC 0.67 +/- 0.04 (CNN), 0.64 +/- 0.04 (ResNet-18), and 0.62 +/- 0.04 (XGBoost). All three FLIO models exceeded the age-only classifier in all T2DM classification tasks, whereas adding age to the FLIO models did not improve model performance. Conclusions: FLIO-derived {tau}CMM maps capture retinal signals associated with diabetes status that exceed what age alone provides, but yield modest classification performance with current artificial intelligence models. These findings highlight both the potential and the challenges of using FLIO for early metabolic screening and monitoring, informing future development of clinically applicable imaging biomarkers.

research.abstract: Tetrigidae is an early-branching family of Caelifera whose species live on damp ground, feed largely on mosses, algae and detritus, and often show wing and pronotum polymorphism. Which chemosensory and detoxification genes underlie this lifestyle is unknown. We generated an Oxford Nanopore PCR-cDNA transcriptome from a pooled sample of adult Hyboella guangxiensis (4.25 million full-length reads) and used it, together with protein homology, to filter the 17,996 machine-learning gene models of its chromosome-level genome to 15,338 supported genes without loss of BUSCO completeness. For nine families (OBP, CSP, IR, SNMP, P450, CCE, GST, UGT, ABC), full-length transcripts corrected 28 of 447 loci, including split and fused models, and brought protein lengths into agreement with orthologs of the sister species Bolivaritettix circocephalus (paired Wilcoxon p = 0.00066). Only 251 loci were supported by complete-ORF transcripts, and 101 had no full-length reads at all. Reconciliation of family phylogenies across eleven orthopteran genomes assigned 119 well-supported duplications to the Tetrigidae stem branch, dominated by P450 (42), UGT (27) and ABC (22) genes, and identified 63 homologous groups restricted to Tetrigidae. Five lineage-specific groups detected as transcripts in adults were validated at the genome level in four non-tetrigid outgroups: a CYP301A-like array, a Tetrigidae-specific UGT clade, two Tetrigidae-specific chemosensory proteins, a CYP9E2-like array and an esterase FE4-like array. Branch-site tests found episodic selection on some members of the UGT and CYP301A-like groups and in 7 of 28 recent paralog pairs, but not in the CYP9E2-like, FE4-like or CSP groups. These genes are candidates for the cuticular, chemosensory and dietary adaptations of pygmy grasshoppers to be tested with tissue-resolved data, whereas no family member could be linked to wing polymorphism.

research.abstract: Background Tuberculosis (TB) remains a major global infectious disease, and novel host-derived biomarkers are needed to improve diagnosis. Circulating microRNAs (miRNAs) are promising biomarkers due to their stability and immune regulatory functions; however, clinically validated TB-associated miRNAs remain limited. This study aimed to identify circulating miRNAs associated with active pulmonary TB. Methods This study included 90 participants: active pulmonary TB (n=30), cured TB (n=30), and healthy controls (n=30). Candidate miRNAs were screened by pooled plasma miRNA profiling and further examined using three publicly available miRNA datasets. Circulating miR-26b-5p was quantified by RT-qPCR. Associations with active TB status were assessed using logistic regression, and discriminatory performance was evaluated by ROC analysis. Putative miR-26b-5p target genes and enriched pathways were explored using bioinformatic analyses. Results Microarray screening identified 108 candidate miRNAs, and cross-dataset analysis identified miR-26b-5p as the only overlapping candidate with consistent downregulation. Circulating miR-26b-5p was lower in active TB and higher in the clinically cured group. It remained associated with active-TB status after adjustment for BMI and PLR. miR-26b-5p showed an AUC of 0.867, while the combined model achieved an AUC of 0.956. Bioinformatic analysis identified 74 putative genes, with EP300, GSK3B, and PTEN as network hubs and PI3K-Akt among the enriched pathways. Conclusion Circulating miR-26b-5p was associated with active pulmonary TB and showed preliminary discriminatory value, supporting its further evaluation as a candidate host-response marker.

research.abstract: Abstract Human Satellite 1B (HSat1B) remains one of the least characterized classical human satellite DNAs, despite its massive abundance on the human Y chromosome. Its tripartite ∼2.5 kb monomer - comprising an AluY fragment, a GC-rich unit (here named H1B) and an AT-rich block - points to an evolutionary origin tightly linked to transposable elements (TEs). Here, we present the first comprehensive comparative genomic, phylogenetic, and transcriptional characterization of HSat1B across 10 primate species using Telomere-to-Telomere (T2T) and chromosome-scale long-read assemblies, combined with DNA-FISH, RNA-FISH and long-read transcriptomic analyses. We demonstrate that while canonical tandem HSat1B arrays are restricted to Homininae (human, chimpanzee, bonobo, and gorilla), the core H1B unit and its structural variants (H1Bsv1 and H1Bsv2) occur across all 10 primate genomes, including strepsirrhines (lemur). This indicates that the H1B sequence predates the assembly of the composite HSat1B monomer by at least 60 million years. H1B variants consistently map within TE-rich genomic contexts, supporting a stepwise, TE-mediated model of satellite diversification and mobilization. Within Homininae, humans exhibit a dramatic lineage-specific expansion driven by Yq12 amplification (∼14.2 Mb; 92% of total genomic content), whereas non-human great apes carry smaller, highly polymorphic autosomal and Y-linked arrays. Finally, we show that H1B-containing sequences are transcriptionally active in human and gorilla nuclei via RNA-FISH and characterize heterogeneous H1B/ Alu chimeric non-coding transcripts in the human male germline. Collectively, our findings uncover the birth and Homininae-specific expansion of a composite satellite DNA seeded by an ancient primate sequence module and sculpted by transposable elements.

research.abstract: Abstract Transposable elements (TEs) are major drivers of genomic diversity, yet understanding their mobility and functional impact requires their accurate description in genomes. TE annotation is still typically performed genome-by-genome. TEs are often shared between some members of the same or closely related species. Hence, TE annotation with a library from a single reference misses families absent from that assembly, whereas building independent per-genome libraries fails to consistently surface shared TEs, hindering comparison. Here, we present Earl Grey ParTEA, a fully automated Snakemake pipeline extending the functionality of Earl Grey for comparative TE annotation across genome panels. ParTEA builds a single non-redundant TE library from all input genomes, resolves chimeric consensus sequences, and uses this shared library to annotate every genome, enabling direct comparison of TE family diversity, abundance, shared and private content, and activity landscapes. Optional modules provide TE library saturation analysis, BUSCO-based assembly quality control, and phylogenetic ordering of outputs. We applied ParTEA to sets of genomes spanning evolutionary scales: ten Arabidopsis thaliana accessions, ten Drosophila species, and ten species spanning the fungal kingdom. The Drosophila TE library expanded from 343 to 1,852 curated families including a previously missed rolling circle element with over 6,000 copies in D. miranda . The proportion of TE families shared across all genomes was highest within A. thaliana (97.3%), 37.7% across Drosophila species and only 0.5% across the set of fungi. ParTEA is available through Bioconda and represents a computationally efficient reproducible framework for comparative TE analysis in the era of large-scale genome analyses.

research.abstract: Abstract Background Retinopathy and age-related macular degeneration (AMD) are the most common findings on fundus photographs of older adults, yet their frequency, correlates and visual consequences have been estimated in separate samples. We compared them in a national survey that graded both from the same images. Methods We analyzed 5593 adults aged ≥40 years in the US National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey 2005–2008 with photographs gradable for both conditions. We estimated survey-weighted prevalence, fitted identically specified logistic models for retinopathy (participants with diabetes) and AMD (full sample), and compared presenting visual impairment (better-eye acuity worse than 20/40) and self-rated vision across four groups: neither condition, retinopathy only, AMD only, and both. Results Retinopathy was more prevalent than AMD (9.54% [95% confidence interval (CI) 8.52–10.56] vs 6.52% [5.54–7.50]); AMD overtook it only from age 70 years. In participants with diabetes, retinopathy was associated with HbA1c (odds ratio [OR] 1.54 per percentage point; 1.33–1.78) and male sex (1.54; 1.10–2.17). AMD was associated with age (OR 1.09 per year; 1.07–1.11) and was less common in non-Hispanic Black adults (0.48; 0.33–0.71). Presenting impairment affected 4.91% of participants with neither condition, 7.09% with retinopathy only, 14.57% with AMD only and 26.15% with both. After age adjustment, impairment remained associated with AMD only (OR 2.23; 1.54–3.23) and both conditions (4.09; 2.28–7.37) but not retinopathy only (1.32; 0.91–1.90). Neither retinopathy nor diabetes was associated with AMD. Self-rated vision agreed poorly with measured impairment (κ = 0.15): only 12% of impaired participants rated their vision poor or very poor. Conclusions Retinopathy is the more frequent retinal finding in US adults aged ≥40 years, but AMD carries more of the measured visual impairment, independently of age. Grading diabetic screening photographs for AMD, and measuring acuity rather than asking about vision, would reach more people who see poorly.

research.abstract: Abstract Atherosclerotic plaque vulnerability drives ischemic cardiovascular events, yet the cellular and molecular signatures distinguishing symptomatic from asymptomatic human plaques remain poorly defined. Here, we compared 53 symptomatic and asymptomatic human carotid plaques using single-nucleus (snRNA-seq; 17 samples, 19,100 nuclei; AtherOMICS biobank) and single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq; 36 samples, 68,983 cells; four public datasets), analysed independently and combined by meta-analysis. Across sequencing approaches, symptomatic plaques showed cell-state shifts toward later or terminal states in osteochondrogenic smooth muscle cells (SMCs) and CD4⁺ T cells, as well as transcriptional changes toward inflammatory and epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT) in endothelial cells (ECs), T cells, and fibroblasts. Nuclear profiling uncovered a depletion of fibroblasts in symptomatic plaques, marked by downregulation of RGS5 . Integrating these transcriptomic signatures with genome-wide association data for coronary, cerebrovascular, and peripheral atherosclerotic disease, we found that genetic risk was enriched primarily in vascular wall cells (SMCs, fibroblasts, ECs), rather than immune cell types. The analyses further nominated higher TWIST1 expression in ECs (colocalized with risk across four atherosclerotic phenotypes), lower GUCY1A1 expression in fibroblasts and macrophages, and higher MRAS expression in T cells as candidate driver mechanisms linking genetic risk to symptomatic plaque transition. These findings provide novel insights into cellular and molecular phenotypes associated with plaque vulnerability and identify potential driver mechanisms of symptomatic plaque transformation that could inform therapeutic development.

research.abstract: Abstract Objective To describe the role of hysterectomy in modifying the major atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease risk factors. Data sources PubMed, Cochrane Library, Embase, and ScienceDirect were searched from database inception to March 10, 2026. Study eligibility criteria Full-text randomized controlled trials, case-control studies, cross-sectional studies, cohort studies, case series, and experimental studies reporting new-onset cardiovascular events, diabetes mellitus, hypertension, dyslipidemia, or other metabolic effects following hysterectomy were eligible. Reviews and book chapters were excluded. Study appraisal and synthesis methods Study selection and data extraction were performed independently by multiple reviewers with conflicts resolved by consensus. Cohort study quality was assessed with the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale; a modified version assessed cross-sectional studies. Meta-analyses were performed using a generic inverse-variance random-effects model for each outcome, stratified by study design (cross-sectional versus cohort) and effect measure (adjusted odds ratio, adjusted hazard ratio, or relative risk). Narrative synthesis was performed for outcomes not meeting criteria for meta-analysis. Results Twenty studies (11 cohort, 8 cross-sectional, 1 mixed design) were included after screening 18,337 records from four databases. Hysterectomy was associated with significantly increased risk of hypertension (cross-sectional odds ratio 1.32, 95% confidence interval 1.18– 1.48; cohort hazard ratio 1.19, 95% confidence interval 1.09–1.30), diabetes (cross-sectional odds ratio 1.21, 95% confidence interval 1.11–1.32; cohort hazard ratio 1.20, 95% confidence interval 1.13–1.29), hyperlipidemia (hazard ratio 1.21, 95% confidence interval 1.13–1.29), obesity (odds ratio 1.24, 95% confidence interval 1.03–1.50), and metabolic syndrome (odds ratio 1.24, 95% confidence interval 1.08–1.44). Conclusions Hysterectomy is associated with increased risk of hypertension, diabetes, hyperlipidemia, obesity, and metabolic syndrome, key modifiable atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease risk factors. Active cardiovascular risk assessment and follow-up may be warranted for women who undergo hysterectomy, particularly at a young age.

research.abstract: Abstract Background Cultivated peanut ( Arachis hypogaea L.) is an allotetraploid crop (2n = 4x = 40) with an AABB genome that preserves extensive synteny between its two subgenomes. This characteristic, along with the availability of multiple genomic resources, provides a valuable framework for the comprehensive characterization of gene families and for inferring their evolutionary dynamics. Here we report a genome-wide analysis of the Dof transcription factor family in peanut (AhyDof), including phylogenetic inferences, gene structures, chromosomal locations, patterns of gene duplication, and expression analysis. Results ​A total of 66 non-redundant Dof genes (AhyDofs) were identified and unevenly distributed across the A and B subgenom​es. Comparative analyses revealed extensive conservation of gene structure, protein motifs, and chromosomal localization among homeologous genes inherited from the diploid progenitors, indicating that allopolyploidization contributed to family expansion while having a limited impact on gene diversification. Phylogenetic analyses placed AhyDofs within the four major angiosperm Dof lineages, supporting the evolutionary conservation of this family across flowering plants. Synteny analyses further identified chromosomal rearrangements and tandem duplication events contributing to the current composition of the AhyDof repertoire. Most notably, we discovered a novel group of six Dof genes associated with previously undescribed Pack-MULE transposons, designated AMuD, providing the first evidence of Pack-MULE-mediated transduplication in the genus Arachis . Structural and phylogenetic analyses suggested that these elements originated from non-autonomous MULEs and captured an ancestral Dof gene related to AhyDof-15.3. The dN/dS rate analysis suggested that transduplicated genes may have evolved under selective constraint, potentially indicating that functional constraints were maintained after mobilization. Comparative genomic analyses, PCR assays across diploid species, and Oxford Nanopore sequencing data suggested that AMuD elements originated within the B–F–K lineage of section Arachis and were maintained during peanut domestication and diversification. Promoter analyses revealed distinct cis-regulatory architectures among AMuD-derived genes, while transcriptomic data demonstrated their transcriptional activity, particularly in reproductive tissues. Conclusions The evolution of the peanut Dof repertoire in peanut was shaped by multiple mechanisms, including polyploidization, chromosomal rearrangements, tandem duplication, and lineage-specific Pack-MULE-mediated transduplication. The discovery of AMuD elements reveals a previously undescribed mechanism contributing to the diversification of regulatory genes in Arachis and provides new insights into the evolutionary dynamics of plant transcription factor families.

research.abstract: Efficient evaluation of sequence data likelihoods and their high-dimensional gradients on phylogenetic trees improves inference under both maximum-likelihood and Bayesian frameworks. Here, we present BEAGLE 4.1, a high-performance library for statistical phylogenetics that incorporates new algorithms to evaluate these gradients on phylogenetic trees. We also provide new hardware implementations for both likelihoods and gradients supporting ARM NEON intrinsics and optimized matrix multiplication units -- called tensor cores -- on NVIDIA graphics processing units (GPUs). We benchmark the performance scaling of the library across a number of patterns and taxa on multi-core CPUs and GPUs, and compare the speedup afforded by NVIDIA and AMD GPUs as well as performance scaling with an increasing number of GPUs. We show that multi-core CPU implementations provide up to a fourfold speedup over single-threaded CPU implementations and up to an tenfold speedup for nucleotide and codon models, respectively, with performance generally improving as the number of taxa and site patterns increases. GPUs outperform multi-threaded CPU implementations for a realistic number of patterns, even for nucleotide models with a small state-space size of 4, while for codon models they provide substantially higher performance gains even for a single pattern or four taxa. Tensor cores on GPUs provide up to 2-fold speedup relative to standard CUDA cores for codon models. Using NEON instructions on ARM CPUs affords up to a $\sim 1.3$-fold speedup over non-SIMD implementation with the speedup going down to 1.1-fold at 8 CPU threads. We provide these new algorithms to evaluate the gradient and efficient hardware implementations for both likelihood and gradient calculations through BEAGLE 4.1, such that they can be readily integrated into phylogenetic software packages.

research.abstract: Abstract Background Identifying functional variants that influence human health remains a challenge in human genetics. Conventional genotype-phenotype association studies test millions of variants, imposing a substantial multiple-testing burden as genomic and biobank datasets expand in size and variant diversity. Additionally, the contribution of structural variation, which is a substantial driver of genetic diversity, remains underexplored in these studies. Signatures of recent positive selection offer a powerful biological basis for prioritizing potentially functional variation, although demographic history can confound their detection and interpretation in these analyses. Results We performed evolution-guided association mapping using long-read genomes from 1,027 self-identified Black or African American participants in the All of Us Research Program and short-read genomes from an additional 38,552 matched participants of African-ancestry. Using demography-calibrated inferences, we identified 228 genomic regions with local ancestry enrichment or depletion and 1,616 candidate loci showing putative recent positive selection signals. These loci were enriched for genic and regulatory sequences, as well as previously reported eQTL, sQTL, and GWAS associations. Leveraging the resolution of the long-read data, we mapped 15 structural variants to these candidate loci, including 10 located within 1,000 base pairs of putative cis -regulatory enhancers. Admixture- and selection-based phenome-wide association testing identified 13 and 446 nominal associations, respectively, 17 of which remained significant following replication and meta-analysis. Conclusions Our results support the use of evolutionary signatures as a robust framework for uncovering clinically relevant variation, including structural variants, in underrepresented populations.

research.abstract: ABSTRACT Background Malignant effusions are clinically accessible yet underutilized sources of metastatic tumor cells. However, abundant background immune cells complicate tumor cell isolation and molecular characterization. We integrate AI-powered single-cell imaging and morphology-guided label-free tumor cell enrichment with genomic profiling to characterize phenotypic and genomic heterogeneity in malignant effusions. Methods We applied a pre-trained deep learning model to brightfield images of single cells from malignant effusions of 10 patients with metastatic breast cancer to extract morphological features, quantify tumor cell fraction (TCF), and guide label-free microfluidic enrichment. We profiled copy-number alterations and somatic mutations in enriched tumor cell fractions and compared them with available matched effusion cell-free DNA and solid tumors. Results AI-powered single-cell morphological analysis identified putative tumor cells in all 10 patients (median TCF, 5.4%; range, 0.51–15.8%; n = 25 samples). AI estimates of major immune-cell populations varied across patients and samples and correlated with flow cytometry measurements (n = 21 paired samples, Pearson r = 0.69–0.75). Unsupervised analysis identified four tumor cell morphotypes, revealing intra- and inter-patient morphological heterogeneity and longitudinal variation in morphotype composition. Genomic profiling of enriched tumor cell fractions by low-pass whole-genome sequencing (n = 26 samples) and whole-exome sequencing (n = 24 samples) identified copy-number alterations and somatic mutations, with tumor fraction influencing genomic signal strength. Comparisons of genomic profiles from tumor cell-enriched fractions with matched effusion cell-free DNA and solid tumors revealed shared genomic alterations, providing orthogonal support for tumor origin and relatedness, while differences across analytes revealed genomic divergence and tumor heterogeneity. Conclusion AI-powered analysis leverages single-cell morphology for tumor cell identification and label-free enrichment, while integration with genomic profiling enables simultaneous interrogation of phenotypic and genomic heterogeneity in malignant effusions. This approach expands the potential of malignant effusions for liquid biopsy applications and biomarker development and discovery.

research.abstract: ABSTRACT Importance Influenza causes substantial morbidity in children, yet Canadian data on influenza vaccine effectiveness (VE) in preventing emergency department (ED) visits and hospitalizations are limited. Objective To estimate VE against influenza-associated ED visits and hospitalizations among children during the 2024-2025 and 2025-2026 seasons. Design Test-negative case-control design. Setting Fourteen Canadian pediatric tertiary-care hospitals participating in the Surveillance Program for the Rapid IdeNtification and TracKing of Infectious Diseases in kidS (SPRINT-KIDS) network. Participants Symptomatic children aged 6 months to <18 years tested for influenza from October 27, 2024, to June 7, 2025, and from November 2, 2025, to June 13, 2026. Exposure At least one dose of current-season influenza vaccine. Main Outcomes and Measures VE against laboratory-confirmed influenza A or B associated with an ED visit or hospitalization. VE was estimated using multivariable logistic regression adjusted for age, epidemiologic week, site, and high-risk comorbidity. Results The 2024-2025 season included 17,316 encounters (median [IQR] age=41.0 [18.5–82.3] months; 54.0% male), with 4,760 influenza-positive cases (8.9% vaccinated) and 12,556 influenza-negative controls (15.9% vaccinated). The 2025-2026 season included 13,417 encounters (median [IQR] age=33.5 [16.7–74.8] months; 54.1% male), with 4,798 cases (7.6% vaccinated) and 8,619 controls (18.1% vaccinated). VE against any influenza was 47% (95%CI, 40–53%) and 53% (95%CI, 46–59%) in 2024-2025 and 2025-2026, respectively. VE against ED visits was 53% (95%CI, 45–59%) and 57% (95%CI, 49–63%), and VE against hospitalization was 33% (95%CI, 16–47%) and 48% (95%CI, 33–59%) in 2024-2025 and 2025-2026, respectively. VE was lower against influenza A as compared to B in both seasons: 31% (95%CI, 22–39%) vs. 75% (95%CI, 64– 82%) (p<0.001) in 2024-2025; and 42% (95%CI, 32–50%) vs. 64% (95%CI, 55–72%) (p=0.001) in 2025-2026. VE was lower in children aged 10 to <18 years than in those <10 years, particularly among children with comorbidities. Protection against influenza A lasted up to 90 days, whereas it persisted beyond 120 days for influenza B. Conclusions and Relevance Influenza vaccines were moderately effective against pediatric ED visits and hospitalizations in both seasons. Routine vaccination should continue to be recommended to prevent hospital-attended influenza. Key Points Question How effective were influenza vaccines against influenza-associated emergency department visits and hospitalizations among Canadian children during the 2024-2025 and 2025-2026 seasons? Findings In this test-negative case-control study of 30,733 encounters at 14 pediatric hospitals, vaccine effectiveness against any influenza was 47% in 2024-2025 and 53% in 2025-2026, despite antigenically drifted A(H3N2) subclade K predominance. Effectiveness was lower against influenza A than B and among adolescents. Meaning These findings support continued annual influenza vaccination of children, even when substantial antigenic mismatch is anticipated.

research.abstract: In 2023, an estimated 13% of worldwide deaths resulting from antimicrobial resistance (AMR) were due to drug-resistant TB (DR-TB). The World Health Organization (WHO) documented a dramatic, sixfold increase in the number of patients treated with 6-month all-oral (BPaLM) regimens, from 5,653 patients in 2023, to 34,000 patients by 2024, while also documenting an emergence of bedaquiline resistance in real-world cohorts and a lack of efficacy of BCG revaccination in the BCG-PRIME Phase 2b trial against sustained Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection. Concurrently, the M72/AS01E subunit vaccine trial completed recruitment (approximately 20,000 individuals) across five high-burden countries, 11 months ahead of scheduled completion date. The first randomized controlled trial assessing DRTB-HDT host-directed therapy for DR-TB in adults (metformin + dovramilast), conducted at five international sites, is entering the late-stage readout phase. This synthesis of data, covering the period from 2015 through 2026, across six different dimensions includes molecular mechanisms of resistance, novel antimicrobial treatment modalities, host-directed therapy, immunity associated with regulatory compliance, adjuvants to vaccines, and the clinical translation of vaccine candidates. The Molecular-to-Translational continuum is used as a framework for the synthesis, with the regulatory immune function domain (T regulatory cells, myeloid-derived suppressor cells, and check-point axes) linking all five domains. Our central hypothesis is that drug resistance evolution of the microbe and failure of the host to maintain regulatory immunity are interdependent and create a bidirectional relationship with each other. We have identified nine major research gaps, with milestone dates from 2026 to 2030, based on unresolved controversies regarding the bedaquiline resistance catalog and the acquisition versus transmission narrative.

research.abstract: Abstract An increased incidence of childhood type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM) has been widely documented, but its pathophysiological origins are poorly understood. The post-World War II expansion of the plastics industry in the United States and elsewhere coincides with a marked increase in T1DM incidence; however, no pathophysiological mechanism has been proposed that could justify such a temporal correlation. Here, we leverage recent advances in artificial intelligence and protein structure prediction and binding to show that molecular mimicry is a plausible pathophysiological mechanism for plastic fragments to induce onset of T1DM for individuals with certain HLA haplotypes.

research.abstract: Abstract BACKGROUND Active case finding (ACF) in India screens large populations to find few cases. AI-NETRA predicts neighbourhood-level tuberculosis (TB) risk from routine notification data and generates field microplans. OBJECTIVE To compare the yield and efficiency of AI-guided and standard ACF, and frontline acceptability. DESIGN Prospective quasi-experimental evaluation in four TB Units of Pune district, comparing two-week AI-guided sweeps (April to May 2026) with the routine campaign in the same units (December 2024 to January 2025). Primary endpoint: bacteriologically confirmed pulmonary TB per persons screened; secondary: all-forms yield, presumptive yield, referral precision, number needed to screen (NNS) and cost per case. Acceptability: 16 focus groups (n=100) and a survey of 101 ASHAs. RESULTS AI-guided teams screened 66,095 people and confirmed 10 pulmonary cases, against 9 among 177,322 in the standard campaign (rate ratio 2.98, 95% CI 1.09 to 8.29); NNS was 6,610 versus 19,702 and cost per case 66% lower. All-forms detection did not differ (15 versus 32; RR 1.26, 95% CI 0.63 to 2.39); the standard campaign had mobile X-ray. 96% of ASHAs reported finding the same presumptive cases while screening fewer people. CONCLUSION Geospatial targeting raised confirmed yield per person and lowered NNS; total detection did not differ. A concurrent, like-for-like trial is warranted.

items.summary: The emergence of drug resistance continues to limit the long term effectiveness of cancer therapies [1], as tumour cells adapt to therapeutic selective pressure through diverse genetic and non-genetic routes [2,3]. research.abstract: The emergence of drug resistance continues to limit the long term effectiveness of cancer therapies [1], as tumour cells adapt to therapeutic selective pressure through diverse genetic and non-genetic routes [2,3]. Despite advances in more potent and next generation inhibitors and mechanism based combination therapies [4,5], durable disease control remains difficult to achieve. Here we tested an alternative strategy: combining multiple inhibitors directed against the same oncogenic driver, each at ultra low doses with minimal individual activity, to delay resistance emergence. In epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) driven cancer models, such ultra low dose same target combinations (ULDCs) distributed individually weak perturbations across multiple inhibitors directed against the same target and achieved substantial growth inhibition in vitro and antitumour activity in vivo despite weak effects of the corresponding single agents. Under similar levels of growth inhibition (~50%), single-agent EGFR inhibitors generated resistant outgrowth, whereas a five drug ULDC delayed resistance emergence. Increasing the number of inhibitors further delayed resistance emergence, with no detectable resistant outgrowth observed for combinations containing 8 to 14 inhibitors within the experimental timeframe. The five drug ULDC also retained measurable growth inhibitory activity against gefitinib resistant PC-9/GR cells, and resistant cells arising under five drug ULDC treatment exhibited markedly greater reversibility following drug withdrawal than those arising under single agent treatment. Although pharmacological additivity or synergy may contribute to the collective growth inhibitory effects of ULDCs, the divergent long term resistance outcomes observed under similar levels of growth inhibition indicate that resistance behaviour is not determined by inhibitory strength alone. Instead, our findings support a model in which increasing same target inhibitor diversity progressively constrains the adaptive trajectories available during resistance evolution, while therapeutic perturbation architecture may also influence the stability of resistant states that emerge. More broadly, these findings support the concept of same target collective suppression, in which multiple individually weak perturbations directed against the same target can collectively produce substantial antitumour activity and constrain resistance evolution across multiple stages. We propose that increasing same target inhibitor diversity may restrict accessible adaptive trajectories, while therapeutic perturbation architecture may also influence the stability of resistant states.

research.abstract: UNLABELLED: The emergence of drug-resistant Mycobacterium tuberculosis strains presents a significant challenge to tuberculosis (TB) control programmes worldwide, particularly in high-burden countries, such as Pakistan. This study characterises the genomic diversity and drug resistance mutation profiles of M. tuberculosis isolates from Khyber Pakhtunkhwa using whole-genome sequencing (WGS). A total of 35 clinical M. tuberculosis isolates underwent WGS. Sequence data were quality-filtered and mapped to the H37Rv reference genome, characterising variants, including single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs). Lineage classification, drug resistance profiling, and identification of resistance mutations were performed using TB-Profiler software. SNP-based clustering was used to infer recent transmission events. All four major M. tuberculosis lineages (L1-L4) were detected; however, more than half of the isolates belonged to lineage L3 (CAS, n = 19; 54.3%). Almost all isolates were drug-resistant (34/35), including pre-extensively drug-resistant (pre-XDR, n = 15; 42.9%) and multidrug-resistant (MDR, n = 14; 40.0%) strains. The most frequent resistance-associated mutations included katG S315T (27/35) and inhA c.-777C > T (4/35) for isoniazid resistance, rpoB S450L (24/35) for rifampicin resistance, embB M306I/V (18/35) for ethambutol resistance, and gyrA D94G (8/35) and A90V (5/35) for fluoroquinolone resistance. Compensatory mutations were observed in rpoC and ahpC. Mutations associated with bedaquiline and clofazimine resistance (mmpR5 c.140dupA, c.138_139dupTG) were detected in single isolates. Interestingly, one isolate exhibited a deletion encompassing mmpR5, mmpL5, and mmpS5, potentially increasing bedaquiline susceptibility. Phylogenetic analysis using 6,635 genome-wide SNPs identified two transmission clusters with < 9 SNPs differences, suggesting ongoing local transmission. These results highlight the presence of drug-resistant M. tuberculosis strains in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, encompassing both globally recognised and novel resistance-associated mutations. Our findings underscore the critical need to integrate WGS into TB surveillance and control programmes in Pakistan to guide targeted interventions and curb the spread of resistant strains. SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: The online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-026-62482-7.

research.abstract: Abstract Background Predictive metabolomics enables efficient early cardiometabolic risk detection, supporting proactive prevention over traditional reactive healthcare approaches. We evaluated the impact of a novel metabolomic risk score (MRS)-based health check on healthcare workload and long-term cost-effectiveness compared with current practices in Finland’s working-age population. Methods A de novo individual-level microsimulation model was developed to estimate labour time and cost-effectiveness when identifying individuals at risk of cardiometabolic diseases (cardiovascular diseases; CVD or type 2 diabetes; T2D). The model used synthetic data on 256,372 Finnish individuals aged 50–54 years without prior CVD or T2D. From a societal perspective, three scenarios were assessed: 1) replacing the standard health checks with MRS-based health checks, 2) replacing standard health checks with MRS-based checks plus enhanced prevention, and 3) comparing enhanced standard checks with MRS-based checks plus enhanced prevention. Outcomes included time required to identify at-risk individuals, incremental cost-effectiveness ratio per QALY gained, and cost-effectiveness acceptability curves. Results MRS-based health checks substantially reduce workload, saving 193,140 hours for nurses and 2,843 hours for physicians over five years. The approach is likely cost-saving across all scenarios, with discounted long-term savings ranging from €27 million to €258 million. In scenarios 1–2, QALYs improve, with gains from 1,316 to 10,813. In scenario 3, no QALY gains are observed, and minor losses occur due to differences in baseline risk stratification. Conclusions MRS-based health checks in primary and occupational care reduce workload and are likely a cost-saving strategy with potential health outcome benefits in identifying individuals at risk of cardiometabolic diseases. Plain language summary Heart disease, stroke, and type 2 diabetes are common and costly health problems. Finding people at risk early can help prevent these diseases. This study looked at a new blood-test-based health check and compared it with current health checks in Finland. Researchers used a computer model based on over 250,000 people aged 50–54. They tested different ways of using the new test and compared time, costs, and health outcomes. The results suggested that the new test can save time for nurses and physicians and reduce healthcare costs. In most cases, it also improved health outcomes. This means that using this type of test could help healthcare services work more efficiently and support earlier prevention, which may benefit both individuals and society in the future. research.abstract: Abstract Background Group B coxsackieviruses (CVBs) are involved in triggering type 1 diabetes. Free bifidobacterial lipoproteins (BLps) prevent CVBs cell infection. Our objective is to isolate free BLps potentially released by bifidobacteria in breast milk and document their bioavailability. Methods Bifidobacterium breve and B. longum were quantified by qPCR in samples donated to the hospital’s biobank (DHM) within two weeks following delivery. BLps were captured onto CV B4, analyzed by SDS-PAGE and competitive ELISA. BLps transport through Caco-2 monolayers was monitored after DHM contact. Titration of anti-CV B IgA was carried out by ELISA. Results Among the 90 enrolled donors, seven were excluded, 68 donated a unique sample and 15 donated multiple specimens (2 to 12). B. breve and B.longum were detected in 93.0% and 32.8% of unique DHM samples, respectively. The two species showed unstable counts in the multiple donation group. Although at highly variable amounts, BLps were readily detected. Free B.longum Lps were found in absence of B.longum itself. The BLps crossed the cell layer within 4h still binding CV B4. Conclusion DHM contained BLps able to cross a cell layer mimicking the intestine still retaining their capacity to bind CV B. It suggested a possible newborn’s systemic protection against CV B4 infection that needs further investigation.

research.abstract: Plant-plant interactions shape community productivity and resilience, yet how genetic variation influences these interactions remains poorly understood. We conducted multi-environment field phenotyping of 200 common bean (Phaseolus vulgaris) lines grown in association with three maize (Zea mays ssp. mays) landraces to characterize the determinants of interspecific interactions. Our results reveal that maize landraces constitute distinct biotic environments, and interactions were strongly asymmetric, with maize acting as the dominant competitor. Bean responses to the identity of the maize partner involved phenology, vegetative development, productivity, and root architecture, and varied across field environments, with no evidence of bean local adaptation. We used genome-wide association to link variation across the bean genome to variation in bean and maize traits, thereby capturing both direct and indirect genetic effects, and tested for maize bean interactions. We identified six genomic regions with indirect effects: three with stable effects across maize partners and three whose effects varied with maize partner identity, including candidate genes involved in neighbor perception and facilitative interactions. Our findings demonstrate that the phenotypic effects of genetic variation extend beyond individual plants, with competitive tolerance modulated by the genetic identity of neighboring plants and the environment.

research.abstract: Codon-based maximum likelihood models are the workhorse of molecular selection analysis, yet standard workflows assume that the input sequence alignment and phylogenetic tree are known without error. In practice, heuristic aligners ignore the genetic code and phylogeny, which packs non-homologous codons into shared columns across insertion-deletion loops and inflates gene-wide false-positive rates above 80%. This sequential division of labor is statistically suboptimal and computationally wasteful. Here, we present WALRUS (Wheatstone Alignment and Likelihood Rate Unification for Selection), a unified engine in HyPhy 3 (https://github.com/veg/hyphy-3) that maps unaligned coding sequences to a coordinate-consistent selection atlas in one run. From a single Inside-Outside likelihood table, the pipeline repairs reading frames, co-estimates a codon alignment and Ohmic reticulate network, models directional base-composition drift, and evaluates eight selection tests (BUSTED-E, aBSREL, RELAX, FEL, dFEL, MEME, Contrast-FEL, and PRIME). Across 10,020 simulated alignments, WALRUS recovers 94.6% of true columns on the 800 INDELible replicates and cuts indel-driven false positives from 44.7%-58.1% to 4.4% under BUSTED (21.1%-21.4% to 1.4% under BUSTED-E). Under Zipfian indel saturation, false positives drop four-fold (33.3%-83.3% to 17.0%-20.5%), while 11,190 avian orthogroup runs execute 6.6-35.8-fold faster and cut housekeeping false positives 13-fold (28-fold on ultraconserved genes) proteome-wide.

research.abstract: Abstract Genotyping, annotating and characterizing TE variation leaped forward with long-read sequencing (LRS) and de novo assembly. LRS techniques also reveal CpG methylation, which enables measuring the impact of TEs on epigenomes and sheds light on the role of TEs as regulatory sequences. Yet, TE genotyping tools discard the valuable allele-specific epigenetic information. We introduce GraffiTE v1.1, the first Nextflow pipeline that genotypes SVs, annotates polymorphic mobile elements (MEI), and maps epigenetic data to TEs using pangenome graphs in one command. GraffiTE v1.1 is designed to map any epigenetic information that is based on LRS stencils, including Fiber-seq. We demonstrate the capabilities of GraffiTE v1.1 by analyzing genomes and methylomes obtained from 20 Quebec residents of French-Canadian descent. In these genomes, TE annotation yields 4,908 Alu, 704 LINE1, 112 SVA and 21 HERVK (HML-2) distinct polymorphic mobile elements (MEIs). We also identify 10 fixed HERVK insertions that vary between solo LTR and provirus, or in proviral copy number. We determine that these MEIs contribute 144,748 additional CpGs not present in the reference. From this, we identify 480 Alus, 67 LINE1s, 12 SVAs and 2 HERVKs in hypomethylated states. We note that Alus and SVAs are more methylated than other LINE1 and HERVK. Lastly, MEIs dating reported a mean of age 1.08 Mya (median: 640 kya) and beta regression identified a moderate demethylating effect of age on MEIs (effect: -0.069 log-odds per log10 years, P < 6.08x10 -19 ). Our results show that the methylation level of a LINE1 MEI is expected to decrease from 86.4% to 80.8% in the first Mya. In conclusion, GraffiTE v1.1 genotypes SVs, annotates MEI, and characterizes their epigenetic state at the scale of populations by leveraging the full potential of LRS. While we showcase its application in human data, the pipeline can be deployed in any model for which a TE library is available.

research.abstract: Abstract Motivation Positive selection is a key evolutionary force in Mycobacterium tuberculosis , driving the emergence of adaptive mutations that influence drug resistance, transmissibility, and virulence of tuberculosis. Phylogenetic trees capture the hierarchical evolutionary relationships among isolates, making them an ideal framework for detecting such adaptive signals. Here, we present a phylogeny-guided graph attention network approach, coupled with a novel method for converting SNP-annotated phylogenetic trees into graph structures suitable for graph neural network processing. Results Using a dataset of 1000 M. tuberculosis isolates, representing the four main lineages, and 206 single-nucleotide variants (75 resistance-associated and 131 neutral) spanning 79 drug-resistance genes, we constructed graphs where nodes represented individual isolates and edges reflected phylogenetic distances. To reduce noise and highlight local evolutionary structure, we pruned edges between isolates separated by more than seven internal nodes. Node features were encoded as binary indicators of SNP presence or absence, and the graph attention network (GAT) architecture comprised two attention layers with a residual connection, followed by global attention pooling and a multilayer perceptron classifier. The model achieved higher accuracy (0.81, AUC 0.82) than a homoplasy-count baseline (0.71) on the held-out test set. Under repeated cross-validation, however, F1 scores did not differ significantly (0.56 vs. 0.58; paired Wilcoxon p = 0.98), reflecting a specificity-sensitivity trade-off: the GAT favoured specificity (0.89), the baseline favoured sensitivity. Applying the model to 138 WHO-classified “uncertain” variants identified 28 high-confidence candidates, including rpoC Ile491Val (rifampicin, compensatory), ubiA Arg240Cys (ethambutol), and rpsA Ala412Val (pyrazinamide). These findings demonstrate the feasibility of encoding phylogenetic trees as graph neural network-compatible structures and the utility of attention-based models for detecting positive-selection signals, supporting genomic surveillance and prioritisation of candidates for experimental validation. Availability and Implementation The source code for the model can be found at https://github.com/linfeng-wang/Phylogeny-Guided_GAT .

research.abstract: Introduction: Diabetes self-management education and support (DSMES) improves glycaemic control, but its benefits often fade once programmes end, and psychosocial outcomes are evaluated less often. We evaluated participant outcomes of the Diabetes and WELLbeing (DWELL) programme, a 12-week psychoeducational self-management programme for adults with type 2 diabetes delivered in four European countries. Methods: In this uncontrolled pre-post evaluation, 605 adults with type 2 diabetes were recruited in the UK, France, Belgium and the Netherlands. Outcomes were assessed at baseline, at programme completion (12 weeks) and at 6-month follow-up. The primary outcome was diabetes self-care (Summary of Diabetes Self-Care Activities); secondary outcomes included HbA1c, weight, BMI, waist circumference, empowerment, illness perceptions, eating behaviour, health status, physical activity and quality of life. Within-person changes were tested with paired Wilcoxon signed-rank tests. Results: Of 605 participants, 453 were assessed at programme completion and 293 at 6 months. Most self-care behaviours improved by programme completion (for example, dietary self-care rose from a median of 2 to 3 days per week), and all seven self-care measures differed significantly from baseline at 6 months (r=0.41 to 0.82; all p<0.001). By programme completion, weight (median 1.25 kg), waist circumference (2.0 cm) and HbA1c (2.5 mmol/mol) had fallen, and empowerment, illness coherence, emotional and external eating, physical and mental health and quality of life had improved (all p<0.001). At 6 months, all metabolic outcomes remained below baseline, although HbA1c had partly rebounded (1.7 mmol/mol below baseline), and most psychosocial gains were sustained. Conclusions: Participation in DWELL was associated with improvements in self-care, metabolic and psychosocial outcomes that were partly sustained 6 months after the programme ended. As an uncontrolled evaluation, the study cannot establish causation, and controlled studies with longer follow-up are needed.

research.abstract: Background: Whole-genome sequencing of Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb) commonly relies on culture-derived isolates, potentially altering the bacterial populations represented. Direct sputum whole-genome sequencing (dsWGS) may better capture lineage composition and within-host variant diversity. Methods: We compared targeted-enrichment dsWGS with WGS of matched culture-derived isolates from participants initiating treatment for rifampicin-susceptible pulmonary tuberculosis in Worcester, South Africa. We assessed sequencing performance, technical reproducibility, sputum-sampling variability, lineage and variant concordance, and resistance-associated variation, and explored associations with baseline clinical characteristics and treatment response. Results: Of 218 clinical dsWGS reactions, 139 passed sequencing quality criteria, yielding 113 eligible baseline sputum-culture pairs. Mixed-lineage infection was detected in 72/113 (63.7%) sputum specimens versus 7/113 (6.2%) matched cultures; 66/113 (58.4%) pairs showed reduced lineage diversity following culture. Permutation analysis indicated preferential retention of Lineage 2 and depletion of Lineage 3 after culture. Technical replicates preserved dominant phylotype assignments (median SNP Jaccard similarity 0.863), while independently collected sputum specimens showed greater variability. Among 38 concordant single-lineage pairs, 35,540/38,311 (92.8%) pair-specific variant observations were shared after filtering and raw-read recovery, while 2,497 (6.5%) were sputum-unique and 274 (0.7%) culture-unique. Discordance was concentrated among variable variants; 88.0% of shared variants variable in at least one specimen had higher allele frequencies in culture. No sputum-unique WHO Grade 1 or 2 resistance-associated mutations were identified in the strain-controlled subset, whereas eight mixed-lineage sputum samples versus three matched cultures harboured such mutations. Higher baseline low-frequency variant burden showed non-significant trends towards delayed culture conversion (log-rank p=0.144) and unfavourable treatment outcomes (log-rank p=0.400). Conclusions: Direct-sputum WGS revealed M. tuberculosis lineage and low-frequency variant diversity that was not fully represented by matched culture-derived genomes, despite high overall genomic concordance. These findings highlight the complementary value of direct-sputum sequencing for characterising within-host diversity, while suggesting that the representation of bacterial populations following culture may vary across epidemiological settings. Further research is needed to improve the accuracy of minority-variant detection and establish the clinical relevance of diversity measured directly from sputum.

research.abstract: Abstract Background The HSP70 family maintains cellular proteostasis and mediates vertebrate responses to environmental stress. The Chinese alligator ( Alligator sinensis ), an ectothermic crocodilian, undergoes winter dormancy characterized by cessation of feeding, reduced activity, and metabolic depression. However, the evolutionary patterns of the HSP70 family across vertebrates and their potential relevance to winter dormancy in crocodilians remain poorly understood. We characterized the HSP70 family across 24 vertebrate species, focusing on the molecular evolution of HSPA12A along crocodilian lineages and its seasonal expression in the hypothalamus of the Chinese alligator. Results Using HMMER- and BLAST-based searches, we identified 355 HSP70 family members, with 11–28 members per species. Phylogenetic, synteny, and subcellular localization analyses indicated that the family is broadly conserved but exhibits subfamily- and lineage-associated divergence. Under two foreground schemes in which the terminal branches of two winter-dormant crocodilians or all four crocodilian species were jointly designated as foreground, HSPA12A showed an elevated relative evolutionary rate and significant evidence of positive selection. HyPhy aBSREL supported episodic diversifying selection on the A. sinensis HSPA12A terminal branch. Public RNA-seq data showed that HSPA12A expression was highest in the hypothalamus among sampled female tissues and was higher in winter than in summer (600.0 and 329.2 TPM, respectively). Western blotting and immunofluorescence analyses showed descriptive differences between the examined specimens, with higher HSPA12A protein abundance and a higher density of cells double-positive for anti-HSPA12A antibody immunoreactivity and NeuN in winter. Because each RNA-seq, western blotting, and immunofluorescence comparison included only one biological specimen per season, these observations were treated as descriptive, and no inferential statistical comparisons were performed. Conclusions The vertebrate HSP70 family is broadly conserved but shows differentiation among subfamilies and lineages. The evolutionary analyses indicate a broader crocodilian-lineage-associated pattern of HSPA12A evolution that cannot be attributed specifically to winter dormancy. Separately, the descriptive transcriptomic and preliminary protein-level observations provide a basis for considering HSPA12A as a candidate for further investigation in relation to winter physiology in the Chinese alligator. These findings do not establish winter dormancy as the selective driver of HSPA12A evolution, and its biological function and causal role remain to be determined.

research.abstract: Camelids have evolved remarkable physiological adaptations enabling survival in extreme desert environments, yet the genomic basis of these traits remains incompletely understood. We conducted a comparative genomic analysis across eleven mammalian species, including three Old World camels, four New World camels, two additional artiodactyls (pig, cattle), and two outgroups (human, mouse), to identify lineage-specific molecular signatures of adaptation. Using OrthoFinder, we constructed orthologous gene families and identified 11,861 single-copy orthologs across all species. We detected significant copy-number changes in cytochrome P450 gene families, with expansion of CYP2J and contraction of CYP4F in the camelid ancestor, suggesting a shift toward anti-inflammatory eicosanoid signaling. Branch-site analyses identified 47 high-confidence positively selected genes in Old World camels, including HACD3, a fatty acid elongation enzyme harboring an ultraconserved substitution (D270N). Structural modeling and conservation analysis suggest that this substitution may hypothetically alter protein conformation, but this prediction awaits experimental validation. Tissue-specific RNA-seq analysis confirmed that HACD3 is expressed in camel kidney and liver, tissues central to lipid metabolism and water conservation. Systematic screening for inactivating mutations identified ten high-confidence pseudogenized genes, including CES3, CPA3, and PLA2G2F, enriched in lipid metabolism and epidermal pathways. The adaptive significance of these losses is currently hypothetical and inferred from homologous gene studies in mice and humans; because some of the cited genes are paralogs rather than orthologs, and because mouse and human phenotypes may not transfer to camels, these inferences are hypothesis-generating only and do not establish camel gene function. Experimental validation confirmed pseudogenization of TAS2R16, and cell-based calcium-signalling assays showed that the camel receptor fails to respond to salicin. This establishes loss of receptor function but not its adaptive significance; both dietary-breadth and neutral (relaxed-selection or drift) explanations remain compatible with the data. For CES3, CPA3, and PLA2G2F, functional consequences in camels remain unverified and require camel-specific experimental validation. Collectively, these results provide a comprehensive framework of gene family evolution, positive selection, and gene loss underlying desert adaptation in camelids, while highlighting that expression patterns are correlative only and do not demonstrate that the identified variants alter protein function or physiology.

research.abstract: Abstract Background AI chatbots now give people with diabetes diet advice, but whether those foods can be bought near home is rarely checked. Methods In a cross-sectional ecological study of 11,974 California and Michigan census tracts, I linked diabetes prevalence (CDC PLACES 2025) with two USDA food-access maps: all SNAP-authorized stores (2025) and large grocery stores only (2019). I identified double-burden tracts (high diabetes and low income/low access) and hidden food deserts (low access to large grocery stores, but not to any SNAP store). In a pilot, ChatGPT, Gemini, and Claude generated meal plans for the same person across 20 high-diabetes tracts in Metro Los Angeles and Metro Detroit; I scored whether advice was healthy and whether foods were sold at nearby store types. Results Double-burden tracts were few (71 in California, 19 in Michigan), almost none in the two metros. Food-desert tracts had a 1.5 percentage-point higher diabetes prevalence (95% CI, 1.0–2.0). Counting all SNAP stores hid 567 Californian and 329 Michigan food deserts; in Metro Detroit, all 97 disappeared, including 51 high-diabetes tracts with about 19,500 adults with diabetes. Chatbot advice was healthy, but in hidden tracts 30% of recommended foods were not reliably sold nearby; the chatbots barely adjusted. Of 55 places they named, 13% had errors, and most were over a mile away. Conclusions The current USDA map obscures food deserts, especially in Detroit, and AI diet advice barely adjusts for them. AI nutrition tools for diabetes should include a place-aware check built on public food-access data.

research.abstract: Abstract Thienothiazolocarboxamides (TTCs) were discovered as a hit in a whole cell screen for new antituberculosis agents. These molecules were rapidly cidal under both replicating and non-replicating conditions and killed Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb) in macrophages. The heterobicyclic core of this scaffold was essential for activity and resistance to these agents was mediated by loss of EthA, a flavin containing monooxygenase also responsible for the bioactivation of ethionamide. EthA-mediated activation of TTCs in whole cells was found to produce mycothiol adducts and RNAseq profiles revealed a mechanism of action identical to the fungal mycotoxins patulin and nidulalin A. EthA oxidizes the sulfur of the thiazole ring to create a relatively stable sulfenic acid that reacts with cellular thiols. This unique, replication-independent, mechanism suggests the possibility that these molecules may contribute significantly to shortening the duration of tuberculosis chemotherapy.

research.abstract: Abstract In case–control single-cell studies, disease often affects only a subset of cells of a given type within each patient. Comparing all cells from patients with all cells from control donors therefore dilutes disease signals, while donor variation and recorded or unrecorded batch effects can be confounded with disease status. We present IDC (Identification of Disease-associated Cells), which uses this cellular heterogeneity as signal. A mixture of affected and unaffected cells creates coordinated variation among disease-associated genes within each patient, whereas shifts shared by all cells of a donor leave this within-donor covariance unchanged. IDC therefore contrasts within-donor gene–gene covariance between patients and controls to learn disease-associated expression programs without batch labels, then applies positive–unlabeled learning to score each cell’s disease-like state and estimate each donor’s disease burden. IDC also computes, in closed form, gene contribution scores and leave-gene-out cell scores that exclude each tested gene, enabling within-donor differential expression testing and cross-donor meta-analysis without retraining. In simulations, IDC identified affected cells and estimated donor burden more accurately than deep generative and label-refinement methods, remained robust to strong unrecorded batch effects, and detected differentially expressed genes more sensitively than case–control pseudobulk methods while controlling false discoveries. In human pancreatic islets and prefrontal cortex, disease burden in held-out donors separated type 2 diabetes (T2D) from non-diabetic donors in beta cells, and late-stage Alzheimer’s disease (AD) from non-AD donors in astrocytes and inhibitory neurons, while placing prediabetic and early-AD donors at intermediate levels. Genes with the highest IDC contribution scores were more strongly enriched for the KEGG T2D and AD pathways than case–control pseudobulk rankings, and within-donor testing revealed coordinated metabolic, cell-adhesion and synaptic changes along the inferred disease axis.

research.abstract: BackgroundDosing guidance for children with leprosy remains operationally challenging. For children under 10 years of age, current WHO recommendations rely on mg/kg dosing of the three separate components of leprosy multidrug therapy, which are difficult to implement in routine care and may result in inconsistent drug exposures. Weight-banded dosing offers a pragmatic alternative that better aligns with pharmacokinetic principles and existing drug formulations. MethodologyA pharmacokinetic simulation study was conducted to develop harmonized weight-banded dosing regimens for rifampicin, clofazimine, and dapsone in children aged 2 to <10 years. Using the WHO dosing tool, drug exposures across harmonized weight bands were simulated and adult-equivalent systemic exposure (80- 125% of adult area under the concentration-time curve) targeted. Predicted exposures were contextualized against safety reference regimens used in tuberculosis meningitis, multidrug-resistant tuberculosis, and leprosy. An iterative review process involving the WHO Technical Working Group on leprosy in children ensured clinical and operational feasibility. ResultsProposed weight-banded multidrug therapy regimens achieved adult-equivalent exposures across most weight bands. Predicted exposures modestly exceeded 125% of adult levels at the lower end of selected weight bands but remained well below safety benchmarks, namely exposures associated with daily rifampicin therapy for tuberculosis meningitis and clofazimine regimens for multidrug-resistant tuberculosis. Dapsone exposures were comparable to those achieved with current leprosy dosing. The existing 10-14-year-old child MDT blister pack could be used without modification in children weighing 25-39.9 kg and with limited tablet or gel capsule removal in children weighing 6-24.9 kg. ConclusionsA harmonized weight-banded dosing strategy was developed that enables effective, practical dosing of leprosy multidrug therapy in children under 10 years using existing free-of-charge blister packs provided through WHO. This approach improves dosing consistency, supports programmatic implementation, and provides a rational interim solution while child-friendly formulations are being developed. Author SummaryLeprosy continues to affect children in many low-resource settings, yet guidance on how to dose treatment in younger children remains limited. Current recommendations often require clinicians to calculate mg/kg doses, which can be difficult in practice and may not match the oral formulations that are available. In this study, we used computer-based simulations to develop a simplified dosing approach for the three drugs used to treat leprosy. We showed that grouping children into weight bands, rather than calculating individual doses, can achieve drug exposures similar to those seen in adults, where treatment is known to be effective. Importantly, we found that these doses can be delivered using existing pre-packed treatment kits by removing selected dose units, making this approach practical in routine care. This work provides a more straightforward and reliable way to treat children with leprosy, reducing the burden on clinicians and improving access to treatment. However, challenges remain, including the lack of child-friendly formulations and limited data on how these drugs behave in children. Further studies are needed to improve treatment for this vulnerable population.
